constraint_statement: Castle Crydee contains a keep.
paraphrase: A named keep exists within Castle Crydee.
notes: Strong foundational anchor for the project.

constraint_statement: Castle Crydee has walls and towers staffed by guards during severe weather.
paraphrase: The castle shell includes walls and towers that matter operationally.
notes: Useful for outer-shell planning.

constraint_statement: Preparations occur throughout the keep and the town below.
paraphrase: The castle and town are vertically or topographically distinct rather than one flat merged settlement.
notes: Important site-relationship clue.

constraint_statement: A wall behind the stables is a recognizable route or boundary edge.
paraphrase: The stable side includes an exterior wall that can be used as a movement anchor.
notes: Keep as likely service-edge evidence.

constraint_statement: The Duke holds court in the great hall.
paraphrase: The great hall is a major public and noble function room.
notes: Major interior anchor.

constraint_statement: A courtyard gate leads into the active castle grounds.
paraphrase: The castle includes a courtyard-gate movement sequence.
notes: Good circulation anchor.

constraint_statement: A long corridor connects the kitchen and the great hall.
paraphrase: The kitchen and great hall are linked directly by a service corridor.
notes: High-value internal circulation clue.

constraint_statement: Castle Crydee has a west wall with battlements under attack.
paraphrase: A named west wall and battlements exist and should be preserved as orientation anchors.
notes: Potentially critical for later directionality.

constraint_statement: The boys gather in the courtyard for the Choosing and it functions as a large public gathering space inside the castle.
paraphrase: The courtyard must be large enough for formal assemblies and processions.
notes: Supports a broad central court rather than a token pocket yard.

constraint_statement: The Duke's Herald comes onto a balcony overlooking the courtyard.
paraphrase: A balcony or upper watch position must overlook the courtyard from the keep or gate side.
notes: Useful for an upper walkable layer.

constraint_statement: A guard opens the small door in the great gate for the Craftmasters.
paraphrase: The main gate sequence includes a smaller postern or wicket within the larger gate structure.
notes: Strong justification for two exterior openings at the gate.

constraint_statement: The Craftmasters stand at the foot of the broad stairs of the keep and the large oaken doors swing outward.
paraphrase: The keep presents a stair-and-door threshold facing the courtyard.
notes: Major front-of-keep circulation clue.

constraint_statement: A shout goes up from the gate tower when the wounded Princess returns and guards run out.
paraphrase: A gate tower lookout exists and is operationally tied to rapid guard response.
notes: Supports an accessible upper gate walk or tower base.

constraint_statement: Pug climbs three steps to the Princess's small flower garden at the side of the keep and hedges mask most of the courtyard from sight.
paraphrase: A small raised flower garden exists on the side of the keep and is screened from most of the courtyard.
notes: Supports a side-garden room with steps and a bench.

constraint_statement: From the garden Pug can still see the tops of the high walls and guards on the parapets.
paraphrase: The garden sits within visual reach of the castle walls and parapets.
notes: Important for keeping the garden inside the main defensive shell.

constraint_statement: Pug's room in the northmost tower provides him with a shortcut through the kitchen rather than the main doors of the keep.
paraphrase: The northmost magician's tower should connect naturally to the kitchen-service side of the keep.
notes: High-value tower placement clue.

constraint_statement: The Duke repeatedly gathers key figures in the council chamber.
paraphrase: The keep includes a dedicated council chamber separate from the great hall.
notes: Strong justification for a deeper keep room beyond the hall.

constraint_statement: The Duke and his sons turn through a door to their private quarters while the boys cut through a storage room into the kitchen.
paraphrase: Private quarters branch off the keep circulation near a storage-to-kitchen route.
notes: Useful for the southern keep and east service spine.

constraint_statement: Tomas leaves in the direction of the guard barracks.
paraphrase: Guard barracks exist as a distinct destination within the castle grounds.
notes: Supports a west-side garrison block.

constraint_statement: Arutha tells Tomas to fetch a sword from the armory.
paraphrase: An armory exists as an accessible support room within the castle.
notes: Pairs naturally with the barracks wing.

constraint_statement: Kitchen stores are kept in the cellars and giant barrels of ale are hauled out for feasts.
paraphrase: The castle needs cellar storage tied to the kitchen-service network.
notes: Strong case for a playable cellar level.

constraint_statement: Princess Carline is ordered back to the cellars during the siege instead of staying on the walls.
paraphrase: The cellars also function as a refuge space
notes: source_logged
column16: Supports a second cellar room with shelter logic.

constraint_statement: The east wall is named and a broad clearing runs along it while west-wall attacks distract defenders.
paraphrase: The east wall is a meaningful orientation anchor distinct from the west wall.
notes: Important for later siege-state directional planning.
